documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V1.0: PLA Wood
Bambu PLA Wood Safety Data Sheet SDS20250723A16
Bambu Lab Filament Hex Code Table: PLA Wood
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 15 ± 4 MPa, elongation 4.5 ± 1.7 %, bending modulus 1975 ± 140 MPa, bending strength 28 ± 4 MPa, impact 5.6 ± 1.2 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting and glass transition are material properties (ISO 1183, DSC) and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows. Vicat (ISO 306) and HDT (ISO 75) are TDS "Physical Properties" rows under their own thermal.* keys; the TDS does not say how those specimens were made (its p.3 note says "All the specimens were printed", but its test drawings cover tensile, bending and impact only).

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 2360 ± 190 MPa, Z 1770 ± 150 MPa), melt index (29.4 ± 1.7 g/10 min at 210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature ("/"), heat deflection temperature 60 °C at 0.45 MPa, saturated water absorption rate (1.25% at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed, with desiccant), bed surface preparation (glue), retraction length (0.6 - 1.0 mm) and speed (20 - 40 mm/s), max overhang angle (~ 55°), max bridging length (~ 30 mm), spool material (ABS, temperature resistance 70 °C) and spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), suggested annealing (50 to 60 °C, 6 to 12 h), odor, skin hazards, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability and combustion products rows.
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (25 - 45 °C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability, not a filament print setting.

The TDS "Bed Surface Preparation Glue" is a recommended setting, not a stated requirement, so no "requires" relation is written; the material-table wiki's "Glue Required" applies to the Engineering Plate only and is kept in that relation's quote.

The TDS "Support Material: Support for PLA" (p.2) is the compatible_with relation "Support for PLA" (target kind material), left without a target handle: no store product is titled exactly "Support for PLA" (the candidate is support-for-pla-new, "Support for PLA (New Version)"; support-for-pla-petg is "Support for PLA/PETG").

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: model "A16-xx", CLP "Not classified", and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO/IATA) transport. Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values. The SDS number is printed "SDS20250723A16" inside the sheet; the file name reads "SDS20250723SA16".

Source disagreement left to review: bed temperature on the TDS's own bed types (TDS 35 - 45 °C on Textured PEI / Smooth PEI vs material-table wiki 45 - 65 ℃ on those plates for "PLA Metal / Wood / Marble"). The product TDS value is kept.

Source disagreement left to review (drying, other than the oven value stored): printer heatbed drying is 65 - 75 °C, 12 h (TDS, X1 Series), 70-75 °C, 12 h (drying wiki, H/X/P2S/P1S) and 70℃, 12 h (PLA wiki); AMS 2 Pro / AMS HT drying is 45 °C, 12 h (material-table wiki and drying wiki) vs 55℃, 8 h (PLA wiki). The drying wiki's forced-air oven range is 55-65 °C (TDS and material-table: 55 °C).

AMS lite caution left to review: the material-table wiki prose says PLA Wood is "compatible with the AMS but not recommended for the AMS lite" and is "Too brittle", while its own table row, the PLA wiki and the store page ("All AMS Series Compatible") say compatible. Recorded as a conflict on the AMS series relation.

Odor disagreement (no registry key): the TDS gives "Odor Odorless", while the store FAQ (4.Wood-like Smell) and the PLA wiki say PLA Wood emits a mild, natural wood scent during printing (non-irritating, non-toxic).

Marketing prose proves no number: "Feels Like Real Wood", "Matte Finish, Fine Texture", "Integrates Perfectly with Other PLA" and the RFID section (store page) are not stored as values or relations. The page-builder section "Enhance Your PLA Models with Wood Accents" ("Bambu PLA Wood integrates seamlessly with other Bambu PLA filaments like PLA Basic and PLA Matte") is a design suggestion (mixing textures in one print), not a compatibility statement, so no PLA Basic / PLA Matte relation is written.

Hex: all six store colours have exactly one hex cell, matched by the colour name without the code in parentheses (the hex table text layer titles the product "PLA wood"; the rendered page reads "PLA Wood"). The Clay Brown cell's printed hex (#995F11) does not match its rendered colour block (about #F4A925); the printed hex is kept with a conflict note.

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/s5/default/413722048c504e38854120a0a89b14c2.pdf) that was not cached and not read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).

The store FAQ (5.Safety Tips) says the filament "is not food-grade"; the drying wiki (Appendix I) marks drying before use and desiccant protection during use as "Required" for PLA Wood. No registry key holds either.

Adjudication against the second extraction (195 field disagreements of 301 compared), each disputed fact re-read in the cached TDS (5 pages), SDS (pp.2-4, 9, 13-14), hex table (text layer and rendered page), PLA wiki, material-table wiki, drying wiki and store page. Same fact, this file's form kept: the locator wording of every TDS row and hex cell ("p.N, Section › Row"; "p.1, row N, column M"); the Cool Plate and Engineering Plate relation labels (the second extraction's "Bambu Cool Plate / PLA Plate" and "Bambu Engineering Plate" cite the same wiki cells, and its wiki-sourced Smooth PEI and Textured PEI rows are in the notes of the TDS plate relations); one ams_series family relation, which also covers the second extraction's "All AMS Series" (store bullet, no source_url), "AMS" and "AMS lite" rows, with the material-table wiki's AMS lite caution as its conflict; one all_bambu_printers family relation for the open-frame and enclosed printer columns, not two; one standard-nozzle relation (TDS Nozzle Size) and one high-flow relation (material-table wiki row "PLA Wood") rather than six; one "0.2 mm Nozzle" relation on the store bullet (its note quotes the FAQ "Hotend with Stainless Steel Nozzle 0.2 mm" and the wiki row). Kept against it: thermal.heat_deflection_temp the TDS 1.8 MPa row (57 °C), as in every other filament file, the 0.45 MPa row (60 °C) in its test_condition; material.spool_type the store bullet "Basic Reusable Spool" (unverified), since the TDS Spool Material and Spool Size rows give the spool's material and size, not its type; compatible_with, not recommended_with, for the TDS Bed Type plates and for Support for PLA, as in the other filament files. Taken from the second extraction after reading the TDS: extrusion.supported_nozzle_diameters (0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm) from the p.1 Nozzle Size row, a registry key for every product type that the other filament files also fill from that row; compatible_with Support for PLA from the p.2 Support Material row. Not taken: thermal.chamber_temp 25 - 45 °C (a range under a printer-capability number key, see the chamber note), a separate compatible_with "AMS lite" relation (the material-table wiki prose says PLA Wood is "not recommended for the AMS lite"; kept as the conflict on the AMS-series relation) and compatible_with PLA Basic / PLA Matte (marketing section, see above). material.net_weight is written as 1 kg, the TDS's own figure (the merge stores 1000 g, text "1 kg").
